paragraphs: School uniforms in Ireland can cost a lot of money. Now the Government wants to make them cheaper.

Education Minister Hildegarde Naughton will bring a plan to the Cabinet on Tuesday. She wants to ask parents, pupils and schools what they think about uniforms. Then the Government will decide what to do.
One idea is to stop schools asking for jumpers, jackets and coats with a brand name. Parents often have to buy these from one special shop.
The charity Barnardos says a basic uniform costs about €240. Many parents say back-to-school costs are hard for them. Simple uniforms from big shops and supermarkets could save families money.
sentZh: 在愛爾蘭，校服可能要花很多錢。
現在政府想讓校服變便宜。
教育部長希爾德加德・諾頓將在週二把一項計畫提交內閣。
她想問家長、學生和學校對校服有什麼看法。
之後政府會決定怎麼做。
其中一個想法是禁止學校要求有品牌名稱的毛衣、夾克和外套。
家長常常必須在某一家特定商店購買這些衣服。
慈善機構巴納多斯表示，一套基本校服大約要240歐元。
許多家長說開學花費讓他們很吃力。
在大型商店和超市買得到的簡單校服可以幫家庭省錢。

paragraphs: The Government wants to look again at school uniforms in Ireland, because many parents say they cost too much. One idea is to stop schools asking pupils to wear branded jumpers, jackets and coats.

Education Minister Hildegarde Naughton will bring a plan to the Cabinet on Tuesday. She wants a national consultation, which means asking parents, pupils, teachers and school managers for their opinions. She says it will be the biggest review of uniform rules in years.

The charity Barnardos says a basic school uniform now costs about €240, and this does not include branded coats. In a survey in July, 59 per cent of parents said back-to-school costs were a financial burden. Many schools also ask pupils to have a laptop or tablet.

Earlier this year, the consumer watchdog, the CCPC, said many schools make parents buy uniforms from only one shop. It said schools should use simple uniforms with a badge that parents can sew or iron on. Then families could buy them in supermarkets and high-street shops.
The department has already started talking to uniform sellers.
sentZh: 政府想重新檢視愛爾蘭的校服，因為許多家長說校服太貴了。
其中一個想法是禁止學校要求學生穿品牌毛衣、夾克和外套。
教育部長希爾德加德・諾頓將在週二把一項計畫提交內閣。
她希望進行全國諮詢，也就是徵詢家長、學生、老師和學校管理者的意見。
她說這將是多年來規模最大的校服規定檢討。
慈善機構巴納多斯表示，一套基本校服現在大約要240歐元，而且不包括品牌外套。
在七月的一項調查中，59%的家長表示開學花費是一項經濟負擔。
許多學校還要求學生要有筆電或平板。
今年稍早，消費者監督機構CCPC表示，許多學校讓家長只能在一家商店購買校服。
它表示學校應該使用簡單的校服，再配上家長可以自己縫上或燙上的徽章。
這樣家庭就能在超市和大街上的商店買到校服。
教育部已經開始和校服賣家討論。

paragraphs: A ban on schools requiring pupils to wear branded jumpers, jackets and coats is among the proposals in a planned national review of school uniform policy.

Minister for Education Hildegarde Naughton will seek Cabinet approval on Tuesday for a consultation that she says will be the most significant review of uniform rules in years. Parents, students, school management bodies and the wider school community will all be invited to give their views, and the department has already begun talking to suppliers who could be affected.

The move follows growing concern about the cost of returning to school. The children's charity Barnardos estimates that a basic uniform costs €240, excluding branded outerwear, while a July survey by the Irish League of Credit Unions found that 59 per cent of parents regard back-to-school expenses as a financial burden. Many families must also pay for laptops or tablets.

In May, the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission warned that bespoke uniforms sold only by exclusive suppliers place unnecessary financial pressure on families. It recommended generic items with sew-on or iron-on crests that can be bought in supermarkets and high-street stores, as well as the ban on branded coats. These recommendations will be considered if the Cabinet backs the plan.
sentZh: 禁止學校要求學生穿品牌毛衣、夾克和外套，是一項規劃中的全國校服政策檢討所提出的建議之一。
教育部長希爾德加德・諾頓將在週二尋求內閣批准一項諮詢，她說這將是多年來最重要的校服規定檢討。
家長、學生、學校管理機構及更廣泛的學校社群都將受邀表達意見，教育部也已開始與可能受影響的供應商洽談。
此舉是因為各界對開學費用的擔憂日益增加。
兒童慈善機構巴納多斯估計，一套基本校服要價240歐元，還不包括品牌外衣；而愛爾蘭信用合作社聯盟七月的一項調查發現，59%的家長認為開學開銷是一項經濟負擔。
許多家庭還必須負擔筆電或平板的費用。
競爭與消費者保護委員會在五月警告，只由獨家供應商販售的訂製校服，給家庭帶來不必要的經濟壓力。
它建議採用可縫上或燙上校徽的通用款衣物，讓人能在超市和大街商店買到，並建議禁止強制品牌外套。
如果內閣支持這項計畫，這些建議將被納入考量。

paragraphs: Schools could be prohibited from insisting on branded jumpers, jackets and coats under a sweeping review of uniform policy set to go before Cabinet this week.

Minister for Education Hildegarde Naughton intends to seek her colleagues' endorsement on Tuesday for a national consultation, which she has billed as the most far-reaching examination of uniform rules in years. Parents, pupils, school management bodies and the broader school community will be canvassed for their views, and officials have already opened talks with suppliers whose livelihoods may be affected.

The initiative comes amid mounting disquiet over the spiralling cost of the return to school. Barnardos puts the price of a basic uniform at €240, a figure that excludes branded outerwear, while a July survey by the Irish League of Credit Unions found that 59 per cent of parents consider back-to-school outlays a financial strain. Mandatory laptops and tablets compound the burden.

In May, the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission censured schools that oblige parents to purchase bespoke garments from exclusive suppliers, contending that such practices impose needless hardship. It advocated generic attire bearing crests that can be sewn or ironed on, enabling families to shop at mainstream retailers, and endorsed the outright ban on branded coats.

教育部長希爾德加德・諾頓打算在週二尋求同僚支持一項全國諮詢，她將其標榜為多年來對校服規定最全面的審視。
家長、學生、學校管理機構及更廣泛的學校社群都將被徵詢意見，官員也已與生計可能受影響的供應商展開對話。
這項措施是在各界對開學費用不斷飆升日益不安之際推出的。
巴納多斯估計一套基本校服價格為240歐元，這個數字還不包括品牌外衣；而愛爾蘭信用合作社聯盟七月的一項調查發現，59%的家長認為開學支出是一項經濟壓力。
強制購買的筆電和平板更加重了負擔。
競爭與消費者保護委員會在五月譴責那些強迫家長向獨家供應商購買訂製服裝的學校，認為這種做法造成不必要的困苦。
它主張採用可縫上或燙上校徽的通用服裝，讓家庭能在主流零售商購買，並贊同全面禁止強制品牌外套。
